subject: Escalate intro demo into an integration deep-dive — availability and agenda

To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>

Subject: Quick demo next week?

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the conversation at RoboCon — Acme is very interested in evaluating Redwood for our inference layer. Could we schedule a 60-minute intro demo next week (Nov 11-12 afternoons PST)? Main goals: latency SLOs, model switching, and multi-region routing.

Hi Alex — great to hear and glad RoboCon was useful. We can absolutely convert this to a technical deep-dive. Quick notes and options: 1) 90-minute integration deep-dive (recommended) with our infra/SDK lead + a short breakout for your engineers; 2) 60-minute overview + 30-minute optional office hours.

Availability: Nov 11 between 1:003:30pm or Nov 12 between 2:304:00pm PST. If those don't work, we can move to the following week.

Agenda (draft):
- 10m: goals and success criteria (your team)
- 30m: architecture & runtime (Karthik)
- 30m: integration patterns, SDKs & KV cache (Marissa)
- 15m: quantization/throughput tradeoffs (engineering)
- 5m: next steps / POC planning

I've attached a short POC outline and a 90-minute ICS for the deeper format. If you confirm the deep-dive, we'll invite Karthik (runtime), Marissa (solutions), and a PM to capture the mutual action plan.

Also, do you have any compliance checklist items (SOC2, data residency) we should surface ahead of time?

Thanks,

Alex / team 3 glad to join. For the deep-dive I'd like to cover a couple of concrete integration checks so your engineers can validate quickly:
- sample latency profiles with small/medium/large sequences (we can demo Live traces)
- KV cache semantics and how to persist/rehydrate across sessions
- SDK example: token streaming and function/tool call wiring
- quantized model performance and fallbacks to FP model at high-concurrency

Proposed prep: please share an example prompt+sequence length distribution (even a rough token histogram) and any firewall/VPN egress restrictions. That helps me pick kernels and replication config to show realistic numbers.

My availability matches Hannah's: prefer Nov 12 2:30pm PST for a 90-minute block; if travel is tight, Nov 16 (next Tue) afternoon also works.

Karthik
